'''Jevon Carter''' (born September 14, 1995) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for [[West Virginia University]] (WVU). A [[point guard]] for the Mountaineers, Carter was known as one of the top defensive players in college basketball, winning the [[NABC Defensive Player of the Year]] and the [[Lefty Driesell Award]] after both his [[Junior (education)|junior]] and senior seasons, and winning the inaugural Naismith Defensive Player of the year in his final season.

==High school career==
Carter played basketball at [[Proviso East High School]] in [[Maywood, Illinois]]. He played mostly off the ball in high school.<ref name=ringer/> From 2011 to 2012 he played for Team NLP in [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] competition, where one of his teammates was [[Jalen Brunson]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Toohey|first1=Terry|title=Villanova’s Jalen Brunson, West Virginia’s Jevon Carter ready to get reacquainted in NCAA Tournament|url=http://www.montgomerynews.com/sports/pros_and_college/villanova-s-jalen-brunson-west-virginia-s-jevon-carter-ready/article_cfee9d88-92d9-5781-b2ac-a918520e026c.html|accessdate=April 12, 2018|work=Montgomery News|date=March 23, 2018}}</ref> Carter was a three-star recruit and was the No. 299 player in the 2014 class according to 247Sports.com. He received scholarship offers from [[Akron Zips men's basketball|Akron]], [[Dartmouth Big Green men's basketball|Dartmouth]], [[Kent State Golden Flashes men's basketball|Kent State]], [[Lehigh Mountain Hawks men's basketball|Lehigh]], [[Toledo Rockets men's basketball|Toledo]], [[Valparaiso Crusaders men's basketball|Valparaiso]], [[Green Bay Phoenix men's basketball|UW-Green Bay]] and [[Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball|Illinois State]], but committed to West Virginia.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Jackson|first1=Chris|title=An inside look at WVU's two seniors|url=http://www.thedaonline.com/sports/an-inside-look-at-wvu-s-two-seniors/article_e6bceb1c-1767-11e8-9efb-039f9a5bed48.html|accessdate=April 12, 2018|work=The Daily Athenaeum|date=February 12, 2018}}</ref>

==College career==
He converted to the [[point guard]] position at West Virginia, making his name as one of the top defensive players in the [[Big 12 Conference]].<ref name=ringer>{{cite news|last1=Wright|first1=Ryan|title=West Virginia’s Jevon Carter Will Make You Work for Every Bucket |url=https://www.theringer.com/2017/3/22/16041646/jevon-carter-west-virginia-2017-ncaa-tournament-bbaf4502ca8f |accessdate=August 10, 2017|work=[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]]|date=March 22, 2017}}</ref> He was one of the architects of "Press Virginia", coach [[Bob Huggins]]'s defensive scheme that forces many turnovers.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Vingle|first1=Mitch|title=Huggins, WVU players marvel at Jevon Carter after record|url=https://www.wvgazettemail.com/sports/wvu/huggins-wvu-players-marvel-at-jevon-carter-after-record/article_80e32df8-fd7f-5959-af42-d6a269605434.html|accessdate=April 12, 2018|work=[[Charleston Gazette-Mail]]|date=December 2, 2017}}</ref>  Carter became a starter as a sophomore and averaged 9.5 points and 2.3 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Casazza|first1=Mike|title=WVU’s Jevon Carter holds his own in Big 12 full of good point guards|url=https://www.wvgazettemail.com/sports/wvu-s-jevon-carter-holds-his-own-in-big-full/article_b6524488-556c-588d-84cb-b7197bbe7351.html|accessdate=April 12, 2018|work=[[Charleston Gazette-Mail]]|date=February 7, 2017}}</ref>

In Carter's junior season in [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17]], he averaged 13.5 points, 5.0 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game. He received many accolades for his defensive prowess, earning Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year, as well as the [[Lefty Driesell Award]] and the [[NABC Defensive Player of the Year]] as the top defensive player in the country.<ref>{{cite news|last1=|first1=|title=Three Teams Lead Men's Basketball Awards|url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211514295 |accessdate=August 10, 2017|work=[[Big 12 Conference]]|date=March 5, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Anderson|first1=Chris|title=Jevon Carter Named NABC Defensive Player of the Year|url=http://westvirginia.247sports.com/Bolt/Jevon-Carter-Named-NABC-Defensive-Player-of-the-Year-52117034 |accessdate=August 10, 2017|work=[[247Sports.com]]|date=April 3, 2017}}</ref> Following his junior season, Carter declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]], but did not hire an agent.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Payne|first1=Terrence|title=Jevon Carter enters NBA Draft, won’t hire agent |url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2017/04/24/jevon-carter-enters-nba-draft-wont-hire-agent/ |accessdate=August 6, 2017|work=[[Charleston Gazette-Mail]]|date=April 24, 2017}}</ref> Ultimately he decided to return to the Mountaineers for his senior season.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Casazza|first1=Mike|title=Jevon Carter to return to WVU men’s basketball |url=http://www.wvgazettemail.com/sports-wvu/20170522/jevon-carter-to-return-to-wvu-mens-basketball |accessdate=August 6, 2017|work=[[Charleston Gazette-Mail]]|date=May 22, 2017}}</ref>

Prior to the start of the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18 season]], Carter was unanimously named to the preseason All-Big 12 team.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Cooke|first1=Hunter|title=West Virginia’s Jevon Carter voted to Preseason All-Big 12 unanimously |url=http://www.ajc.com/sports/college/west-virginia-jevon-carter-voted-preseason-all-big-unanimously/2IkpNV5dWjhuvhhCyqmNvK/ |accessdate=December 9, 2017|work=[[Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|date=October 12, 2017}}</ref> On November 30, 2017, Carter became WVU’s all-time leader in [[Steal (basketball)|steals]], surpassing [[Greg Jones (basketball)|Greg Jones’]] mark of 252 in a win over [[NJIT Highlanders men's basketball|NJIT]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=|first1=|title=Carter Breaks WVU Steal Record in Tonight's Win |url=http://wvusports.com/news/2017/11/30/mens-basketball-carter-breaks-wvu-steal-record-in-tonights-win.aspx?path=mbball |accessdate=December 9, 2017|work=[[West Virginia Mountaineers]]|date=November 30, 2017}}</ref> On March 3, 2018 against [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]], he became the first major conference player to reach 1500 points, 500 rebounds, 500 assists and 300 steals in a career.<ref>{{cite news|last1=|first1=|title=West Virginia's Jevon Carter becomes first major conference player to reach 1,500 points, 500 rebounds, 500 assists, 300 steals |url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2018-02-24/west-virginias-jevon-carter-becomes-first-major-conference |accessdate=March 10, 2018}}</ref>

On March 12, 2018 Carter was named [[List of Men's Basketball Academic All-America Team Members of the Year|Academic All-American of the Year]] for Division I men’s basketball.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://academicallamerica.com/news/2018/3/12/2017-18-academic-all-america-ncaa-division-i-mens-basketball-team-announced.aspx |title= 2017-18 Academic All-America® NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Team Announced|publisher=College Sports Information Directors of America |date=March 12, 2018 |accessdate=March 12, 2018}}</ref>

On March 27, 2018 Jevon Carter was listed to the Associate Press All-American 2nd Team. He has also been added to the Sporting News 2nd Team, USA Today 3rd Team, the NBC 3rd Team, and the NABC 3rd Team All-American Teams. <ref>http://wvusports.com/news/2018/3/27/mens-basketball-carter-named-associated-press-all-american.aspx?path=mbball</ref> Later that same week, he was added to the 2018 John R. Wooden Award All American Team. <ref>http://wvusports.com/news/2018/3/28/mens-basketball-carter-named-to-john-wooden-all-american-team.aspx?path=mbball</ref> 
He also won the 2018 Senior CLASS Award in NCAA Men's Basketball. This award (''Celebrating Loyalty and Achievement for Staying in School''), given annually, is for the most outstanding senior student athlete in Men's Basketball. Carter is the second player in West Virginia University history to win this award, the first being [[Da'Sean Butler]], who won it in 2010. <ref>http://wvusports.com/news/2018/3/30/mens-basketball-carter-wins-senior-class-award.aspx?path=mbball</ref>

On April 1, 2018, Jevon Carter was named as both the NABC Defensive Player of the Year<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2018-04-02|title=NABC Defensive Player of the Year|url=https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=NABC_Defensive_Player_of_the_Year&oldid=833742387|journal=Wikipedia|language=en}}</ref> and the Naismith Defensive Player of the Year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://naismithtrophy.com/jevon-carter-wins-inaugural-naismith-defensive-player-of-the-year-award/|title=Jevon Carter Wins Inaugural Naismith Defensive Player of the Year Award {{!}} Citizen Naismith Trophy|website=naismithtrophy.com|language=en-US|access-date=2018-05-21}}</ref> Carter also won the NABC Defensive Player of the Year award in the 2016-17 season <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://wvusports.com/news/2018/4/1/mens-basketball-carter-repeats-as-nabc-defensive-player-of-the-year.aspx|title=Carter Repeats as NABC Defensive Player of the Year - West Virginia University|website=West Virginia University|language=en|access-date=2018-05-21}}</ref>, becoming only the 7th player in history to win the award more than once, and the first since [[Hasheem Thabeet]] won in the [[2007–08 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2007-08 season]] and the [[2008–09 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2008-09 season]]. He won the inaugural Naismith Defensive Player of the Year award.
